title: NGINX architecture
summary: A master process supervises event-driven workers that terminate TLS, match config contexts, cache and proxy to upstreams.

nodes.label: Client
nodes.detail: Opens HTTPS connections to port 443. A load balancer in front may prepend the PROXY protocol header so the real client address is preserved.

nodes.label: Config contexts
nodes.detail: nginx.conf is a nested hierarchy of contexts. Directives are inherited downward: http, then server blocks chosen by listen and server_name, then location blocks chosen by URI.

nodes.label: Master process
nodes.detail: Runs privileged: reads and validates the configuration, binds listening sockets, starts workers and handles signals such as reload without dropping connections.

nodes.label: Worker 1
nodes.detail: Each worker is a single-threaded event loop using epoll on Linux. It multiplexes thousands of connections without a thread per connection.

nodes.label: Worker 2
nodes.detail: Workers share the listening sockets inherited from the master. The worker_processes directive (commonly auto) sets how many run, typically one per CPU core.

nodes.label: Worker N
nodes.detail: Workers run unprivileged and share state only through shared memory zones such as cache keys and rate-limit counters, so a crash affects only that worker's connections.

nodes.label: TLS termination
nodes.detail: The worker completes the TLS handshake using the configured certificate and key, then handles plain HTTP internally. Session resumption reduces repeat handshake cost.

nodes.label: Cache
nodes.detail: With proxy_cache enabled, a cacheable response is stored on disk under a key (proxy_cache_key). Repeat requests are answered as HIT without contacting the upstream.

nodes.label: Upstream group
nodes.detail: An upstream block lists backend servers. Requests rotate round robin by default; after max_fails failures within fail_timeout a server is temporarily skipped.

nodes.label: App server A
nodes.detail: An application backend reached via proxy_pass, over HTTP, optionally using keepalive connections to the upstream.

nodes.label: App server B
nodes.detail: A second backend in the same upstream group. If A is marked unavailable, requests go here.

nodes.label: Stream module
nodes.detail: The stream context proxies raw TCP or UDP, with optional TLS termination, for non-HTTP protocols. It also supports the PROXY protocol on listen.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL / Redis
nodes.detail: Databases and caches reached as plain TCP through the stream proxy, so clients can use one stable address while backends change.

steps.title: Accept
steps.text: A client connects to port 443. The kernel hands the connection to one worker, whose epoll loop accepts it without blocking.

steps.title: TLS handshake
steps.text: The worker terminates TLS with the configured certificate, negotiating HTTP/2 if enabled, then reads the decrypted request.

steps.title: Server and location match
steps.text: NGINX picks the server block by listen and server_name, then the best matching location. Its directives decide what happens next.

steps.title: Upstream selection
steps.text: On a cache miss, proxy_pass sends the request to the upstream group. Round robin picks a server, skipping ones past max_fails.

steps.title: Response and cache
steps.text: The response streams back through the worker to the client. If cacheable, it is stored so later requests are served as a HIT.
